why: This checker's default run is over assets that are all correct, so nothing about it going quiet shows up in an exit code: a requirement table emptied, a dimension comparison that no longer fires, a missing file read as a pass — every one of those leaves the run printing the same clean line. The self-test breaks a generated asset tree one way at a time and requires a refusal each time, and the edits below are the ways the checker could stop being able to refuse anything.

mutations.name: the PNG requirements are never checked
mutations.breaks: Every PNG passes because none is opened. Dimensions, alpha and the image data itself stop being checked at all.
mutations.find:
for relative, expected in PNG_REQUIREMENTS.items():
        problems.extend(validate_png(root, relative, expected))
mutations.replace:
for relative, expected in []:
        problems.extend(validate_png(root, relative, expected))

mutations.name: the SVG requirements are never checked
mutations.breaks: The wordmark, the compact mark and the architecture diagram stop being checked for a viewBox or a title, which is how a diagram ends up shipping under the wrong name.
mutations.find:
for relative, expected_title in SVG_REQUIREMENTS.items():
        problems.extend(validate_svg(root, relative, expected_title))
mutations.replace:
for relative, expected_title in []:
        problems.extend(validate_svg(root, relative, expected_title))

mutations.name: the PNG requirement table is emptied
mutations.breaks: The checker is disabled by deleting its input rather than its code — the shape of failure that reads as a clean run over nothing.

mutations.name: the SVG requirement table is emptied
mutations.breaks: The same disabling by deletion, on the half of the table that pins what each diagram is called.

mutations.name: the brand README requirement is dropped
mutations.breaks: The assets can ship with nothing saying what they are for or how they may be used.

mutations.name: the dimension check never fires
mutations.breaks: An asset of any size satisfies its requirement, which is the whole point of naming a size.

mutations.name: the dimension check is made unconditional
mutations.breaks: The comparison is thrown away in the other direction: the checker refuses correct assets, so it is no longer reading what it is comparing against. It is here because a check that always fires and one that never fires are the same amount of information.

mutations.name: the alpha requirement never fires
mutations.breaks: The mascot and the mark can lose their transparency and still pass, which is what puts a white box behind a logo on a dark page.

mutations.name: the PNG parse returns the answer it was expected to give
mutations.breaks: The file is never read: the checker compares the requirement with itself and agrees. This is the edit that would survive every check downstream of it, including the byte flipped with its CRC re-signed.

mutations.name: a missing PNG reads as a pass
mutations.breaks: An asset deleted from the tree stops being a problem, so the checker reports clean over files that are not there.

mutations.name: a missing SVG reads as a pass
mutations.breaks: The same hole on the SVG side, where the architecture diagram the docs embed can simply be gone.

mutations.name: the SVG title check never fires
mutations.breaks: A diagram can carry any title, so a copy of the wrong file passes as long as it is valid XML.

mutations.name: an asset no requirement names goes unnoticed
mutations.breaks: The cross-check against the committed brand directory goes, and with it the only thing making an added asset — or a deleted requirement entry — loud.
mutations.find:
if path.suffix.lower() == ".png" and relative not in PNG_REQUIREMENTS:
            problems.append(f"{relative}: committed but named by no PNG requirement")
mutations.replace:
if False:
            problems.append(f"{relative}: committed but named by no PNG requirement")

mutations.name: the problems are printed and the run exits 0
mutations.breaks: The checker finds everything and reports it, and the exit code says the tree is fine. Nothing that reads only the verdict would ever know.

mutations.name: the script's entry point is neutered
mutations.breaks: The verdict never reaches an exit code at all. A run that did nothing prints no signature, which is how this is told apart from a run that passed.
